entries.reason: The current parser leaves empty scripts as text while Pandoc emits empty nodes. The O/I/P provenance audit found that an example rewrite reversed the original empty-caret contract under a false Pandoc premise; this entry records current output, not verified intent. Double-tilde strikethrough ownership is a separate decision.
Markdown Core retains inherited declarations before occurrence declarations, preserving every duplicate; Pandoc combineAttr instead deduplicates and reprioritizes declarations.

The table syntax is implemented. The normative relative field stores each source interior width divided by their sum. Pandoc stores widths including separators against its default page width. Both original values remain compared; this is a documented semantic width difference, not a missing producer or an AST-only equivalence.

Markdown Core retains every specimen as a document-owned definition in source order, including anonymous and duplicate labels, and stores references by exact id. Pandoc emits example List items and replaces references with derived numbering; those values are not projected away.

This compound reader omits all_symbols_escapable, so successful script escapes also differ because of oracle configuration. An isolated control with that prerequisite agrees. The real contextual difference is that only committed product scripts decode escaped ASCII space to NBSP; outside or failed scripts retain inherited literal spelling.
Every raw Unicode whitespace scalar invalidates unmatched script openers. A subsequent delimiter can open a new candidate immediately.
Character-reference whitespace is decoded content and never a raw-whitespace boundary for script matching. Markdown Core preserves a decoded TAB; Pandoc normalizes it to an ASCII space.

Nonempty script units pair left to right. Two tildes belong exclusively to strikethrough and longer runs are literal. The empty-caret portions also reproduce the historical reversal identified by the O/I/P audit and must not be treated as approved merely because this compound entry is registered.
Complete code tokens own their bytes, including whitespace and script delimiter characters, before the delimiter engine sees them.
Markdown Core reserves every explicit declaration across the whole document before generating anchors; Pandoc allocates this heading before it sees the later explicit heading identifier.
Markdown Core filters every scalar uniformly and has no emoji alias step; Pandoc converts the grinning-face scalar to its grinning alias during GFM anchor generation.
Markdown Core applies Unicode 17 simple lowercase (U+0130 becomes U+0069); Pandoc expands U+0130 to U+0069 U+0307 with full lowercase.
Markdown Core maps each Unicode White_Space scalar to a hyphen, including U+0085 and U+2028; Pandoc removes those two scalars from this heading anchor.
Markdown Core reserves identifiers on every emitted kind before heading synthesis; Pandoc does not reserve the code identifier against its heading registry.

Markdown Core keeps the inherited CommonMark reference-tail adjacency rule, so whitespace-separated occurrences resolve independently; Pandoc combines the first two bracket groups into one full reference.
The shared anchor registry reserves explicit Span identifiers across the whole document before heading synthesis. Pandoc generates the earlier heading before reading the later Span identifier.
Both affixes exclude raw leading and trailing whitespace under the citation module. Pandoc retains a leading suffix space before nested brackets; nested owners and their content remain compared.

The current first author-tail section is suffix inline content, so a later @key becomes a nested authorInText Cite. Pandoc makes it another normal item of the outer Cite. The O/I/P audit flags this grouping/mode choice for semantic review; ordinary bracket-group nesting does not establish the author-tail rule.

An item without a key invalidates the complete bracketed group; the current product leaves its unclaimed keys as raw Text while Pandoc retains authorInText citations. The O/I/P audit flags the blanket literal example against the transactional fallback rule for semantic review.
Generated anchors concatenate the stored, trimmed citation prefix, @key and suffix per item. Pandoc uses the authored fallback spelling with separator spaces; its suffix also retains a leading space.
The key opener precondition forbids a preceding underscore as well as Unicode letters and numbers. Pandoc accepts a citation after underscore.
A nested ordered list must start at one; a rejected marker remains in the existing paragraph under the inherited lazy-continuation rules. Pandoc splits that line into another paragraph.

A non-resolving reference tail does not block a complete bibliography group. Pandoc leaves the first brackets literal and parses their key as authorInText.

The inherited reference-definition grammar registers the authored @a label, but a complete citation group wins over its shortcut. Pandoc parses the declaration-shaped line as a citation followed by text.
List.start always stores the first authored numeral for every variant. Pandoc without startnum replaces that value with one.
Named and nameless containers share one closer rule: the colon run must be at least as long as the opening fence. Pandoc closes with any run of three or more.
The document reserves every explicit anchor before synthesizing heading anchors (P3). Pandoc gives the earlier heading the later div ID as well; Markdown Core allocates reserved-1.

The product retains the authored term-gap compact flag even when the first body contains no top-level paragraph (nested definition list, code or an empty body). Pandoc stores tightness through Plain/Para and has no corresponding flag in these shapes; its projection records null rather than inventing one. All terms and ordered bodies remain compared.
